composition_owner: intergrax/runtime/execution/ (EE owner zone): runtime.py (ExecutionRuntime), boundary.py, nexus_host_execution.py (build_host_task_execution), environment_orchestration_materialization.py (sole production NexusLoop construction), host_orchestration_wiring_bundle.py; legal root start = intergrax/runtime/governance/default_root_execution_launcher.py via RootExecutionLaunchPort

Lab/debug: intergrax/runtime/execution/debug_lab_nexus_loop.py, lab_reference_agent_runtime.py

risks.text: Host-task agent routing drops production_mode: build_host_task_execution() builds a fresh AgentRouter with the default production_mode=False instead of the NexusLoop's setting; HostTaskExecution routes via it whenever task.agent_id is empty. NexusLoop.production_mode itself defaults to False (RuntimeConfig default is True). See finding f1.
AgentRouter falls back to the first routable agent (selection_reason fallback_first_routable) when no capability/best match exists; token appears in no doc and no test. See finding f2.

Several scheduler/worker mechanisms coexist (WorkerRuntime, NexusWorkerRuntime, LongRunningScheduler, CapacityScheduler, AdaptationScheduler, VendorKnowledgeSyncScheduler). Sampled VendorKnowledgeSyncScheduler: it only enqueues on TaskQueue (no execution authority). Others not traced - FRZ-EXE-07 is PASS in checklist; residual is a Campaign B probe, not a defect claim.

Nexus encapsulation confirmed at BASELINE by grep: production importers of intergrax.runtime.nexus outside runtime/nexus and runtime/execution = 0 (only tests under applications/*/tests, intergrax/agents/reference_harness.py docstring mention, prompts inventory string, sandbox isolation_gate string); NexusLoop( constructed only in runtime/execution owner zone.

risks.text: Authority narrowing confirmed in code: mint_effective_delegation_authority raises on over-broad child scopes (E3). Residual: when parent.unrestricted, the child gets exactly the requested scopes without further bound (by design root authority).

Four policy/governance entry points coexist: GovernanceService, PolicyEngine facade, RuntimePolicyEngine, AgentRuntimePolicyEngine. PolicyEngine is documented as a unified facade; whether AgentRuntimePolicyEngine is a separate authority or a provider chain under it was not traced. Hypothesis for Campaign B (FRZ-OWN-04/05).

Governance enforcement is conditional on production_mode / strict execution mode: non-strict hosts get no MSE authorization port and no agent runtime governance; flag semantics are not described in the Tier-3/Foundation docs. See finding f8 (hypothesis).
LabAllowGovernanceService.evaluate returns None (no evaluation) and is used only by lab_reference_agent_runtime.py; acceptable lab scope, labelled in docstring.
